+#ifndef TRITON_ASCEND_SSBUF_CROSSCOREPATTERN_H
+#define TRITON_ASCEND_SSBUF_CROSSCOREPATTERN_H
+
+#include "mlir/IR/BuiltinOps.h"
+
+namespace mlir {
+namespace triton {
+
+/// The shape of the cross-core dependency graph of a module.
+struct CrossCorePattern {
+  /// The number of independent pipelines of the graph.
+  unsigned pipelines = 0;
+  /// The number of entry blocks of the pipelines: the blocks of the
+  /// qualifying chains that no other block of the chains feeds. A pipeline
+  /// that is a single linear chain has one entry; two blocks feeding the
+  /// same block is a merge, and the merge has two entries.
+  unsigned entries = 0;
+};
+
+/// Analyzes the cross-core dependency graph of `module` and reports its
+/// pipelines.
+///
+/// The nodes of the graph are the computation blocks, a block being the pair
+/// of the scope that holds it and its `ssbuffer.block_id`; block ids are only
+/// unique inside a scope. The edges are the cross-core dependencies, the
+/// producer block of a dependency group feeding the consumer block of the
+/// same group. Every edge joins two different cores, so a chain always
+/// alternates the cores: CUBE -> VECTOR -> CUBE -> VECTOR or VECTOR -> CUBE
+/// -> VECTOR -> CUBE.
+///
+/// A chain has to carry the tightly coupled buffers of the validated
+/// pipeline: every transfer of the chain is double buffered and no buffer is
+/// shared by two transfers of the chain, so the chain of `chainLength` blocks
+/// uses 2 * (chainLength - 1) tightly coupled buffers.
+///
+/// One direction of the graph may be carried by several cross-core groups.
+/// The buffers of the direction are the buffers of all of them, and the
+/// direction has to carry the buffers of exactly one transfer, so that every
+/// transfer of the pipeline carries the same number of buffers.
+///
+/// The conditions are computed for the blocks that carry a condition, so the
+/// cross-core blocks of the module that carry a condition have to be the
+/// blocks of one of the two validated pipelines: four of them for the mla
+/// pipeline and five of them for the paged decode pipeline.
+///
+/// Two chains that share a block are two views of the same pipeline and count
+/// once; the chains that share no block are independent pipelines.
+CrossCorePattern analyzeCrossCorePattern(ModuleOp module,
+                                         unsigned chainLength = 4);
+
+} // namespace triton
+} // namespace mlir
+
+#endif // TRITON_ASCEND_SSBUF_CROSSCOREPATTERN_H

+namespace mlir {

+// Loop iteration times info
+struct IterationTimesInfoLegacy {
+  int ifCount = 0;                       // Number of if operations
+  int requiredBuffers = 1;               // Number of required buffers
+  int x = 1;                             // Number of producer buffers
+  SmallVector<scf::IfOp> ifOpsInThisFor; // If operations in this loop
+};
+
+class UpdateLoopIterTimesPassLegacy
+    : public PassWrapper<UpdateLoopIterTimesPassLegacy,
+                         OperationPass<ModuleOp>> {
+public:
+  UpdateLoopIterTimesPassLegacy() = default;
+  void runOnOperation() override;
+  void setConditionInfo(ControlFlowConditionInfo *info) { this->info = info; }
+
+private:
+  ControlFlowConditionInfo *info = nullptr;
+
+  int GetMainLoopIdToLoopOpMap(ModuleOp module,
+                               DenseMap<int, SmallVector<Operation *>> &cmap,
+                               DenseMap<int, SmallVector<Operation *>> &vmap);
+
+  int ComputeMainLoopTimes(
+      DenseMap<int, SmallVector<Operation *>> &loopMap,
+      DenseMap<Operation *, IterationTimesInfoLegacy> &infoMap);
+
+  int UpdateForLoopIteration(
+      DenseMap<int, SmallVector<Operation *>> &cmap,
+      DenseMap<int, SmallVector<Operation *>> &vmap,
+      DenseMap<Operation *, IterationTimesInfoLegacy> &infoMap);
+
+  int collectForOpsAndUpdateMax(
+      DenseMap<int, SmallVector<Operation *>> &map, int id,
+      SmallVector<Operation *> &allForOps, int &maxIfCount,
+      int &maxRequiredBuffers, int &maxX,
+      DenseMap<Operation *, IterationTimesInfoLegacy> &infoMap);
+
+  int replaceForOpCounterInIfOps();
+
+  int UpdateWhileLoopCondition(
+      DenseMap<int, SmallVector<Operation *>> &mainLoopIdMap);
+
+  // Calculate factor = requiredBuffers / x
+  std::pair<int, int> calculateFactor(scf::ForOp forOp);
+
+  // Calculate factor based on intra-core dependencies
+  // Iterates all dependencies and computes the maximum required buffer count
+  // Returns {maxRequiredBuffers, maxX} where:
+  //   - maxRequiredBuffers: maximum (m - n + 1) across all dependencies
+  //   - maxX: the x value corresponding to maxRequiredBuffers
+  //   - returns {-1, -1} on error
+  std::pair<int, int> calculateIntraDepsFactor(
+      SmallVector<scf::IfOp> &ifOps, DenseMap<Operation *, int> &ifOpIndex,
+      DenseMap<Operation *, SmallVector<Operation *>> &deps);
+
+  // Calculate factor based on cross-core dependencies
+  // For cross-core deps: consumer is in current forOp, producer is in another
+  // mainloop with the same id but in a different scope (cube vs vector)
+  // Returns {maxRequiredBuffers, maxX} where:
+  //   - maxRequiredBuffers: maximum (m - n + 1) across all dependencies
+  //   - maxX: the x value corresponding to maxRequiredBuffers
+  //   - returns {-1, -1} on error
+  std::pair<int, int>
+  calculateCrossDepsFactor(scf::ForOp forOp, SmallVector<scf::IfOp> &ifOps,
+                           DenseMap<Operation *, int> &ifOpIndex,
+                           ConsumerProducerMap &crossDeps);
+
+  // Calculate factor based on iteration dependencies (tensor iter_args
+  // dependencies) For iter deps: consumer and producer are IfOps within the
+  // same forOp Returns {maxRequiredBuffers, maxX} where:
+  //   - maxRequiredBuffers: maximum (m - n + 1) across all dependencies
+  //   - maxX: the x value corresponding to maxRequiredBuffers
+  //   - returns {-1, -1} on error
+  std::pair<int, int>
+  calculateIterDepsFactor(scf::ForOp forOp, SmallVector<scf::IfOp> &ifOps,
+                          DenseMap<Operation *, int> &ifOpIndex);
+
+  // Extend for loop iteration count
+  scf::ForOp extendForOpIterationCount(scf::ForOp oldForOp, int ifCount,
+                                       int requiredBuffers, int x,
+                                       IRMapping &mapper,
+                                       SmallVector<scf::IfOp> &ifOpsInThisFor);
+
+  Value computeNewLoopUpperBound(OpBuilder &builder, Location loc,
+                                 scf::ForOp forOp, int ifCount,
+                                 int requiredBuffers, int x);
+
+  scf::ForOp cloneForOpWithNewUpperBound(OpBuilder &builder, Location loc,
+                                         scf::ForOp oldForOp,
+                                         Value newUpperBound,
+                                         IRMapping &mapper);
+
+  int updateCntArgsAfterClone(scf::ForOp oldForOp, IRMapping &mapper,
+                              SmallVector<scf::IfOp> &ifOpsInThisFor);
+
+  void
+  updateMainLoopMaps(Operation *oldForOp, Operation *newForOp,
+                     DenseMap<int, SmallVector<Operation *>> &cmap,
+                     DenseMap<int, SmallVector<Operation *>> &vmap,
+                     DenseMap<Operation *, IterationTimesInfoLegacy> &infoMap);
+};

+

+// RUN: triton-opt --add-control-flow-condition %s | FileCheck %s --implicit-check-not=scf.while --implicit-check-not=arith.select
+
+// A kernel whose cross-core dependency is a CUBE -> VECTOR -> CUBE -> VECTOR
+// chain is recognized by the pattern, but the name of the kernel is in the
+// black list of AddControlFlowCondition. The black list has the priority: the
+// kernel keeps the conditions of the upstream implementation, its main loop is
+// an scf.for and the cores are synchronized with PIPE_S. The normal preload
+// scheme is not used, the implicit checks forbid the scf.while loop and the
+// arith.select of the flags.
+//
+// The dependency chain of this test is:
+//   cube block 0 -> vector block 1 -> cube block 2 -> vector block 3
+
+// CHECK-LABEL: func.func @paged_decode_fd_kernel
+
+// The upstream scheme: the main loop stays an scf.for and the cores are
+// synchronized with PIPE_S.
+// CHECK: scf.for
+// CHECK: hivm.hir.sync_block_wait[<VECTOR>, <PIPE_S>, <PIPE_S>] flag = 15
+// CHECK: scf.for
+// CHECK: hivm.hir.sync_block_wait[<CUBE>, <PIPE_S>, <PIPE_S>] flag = 15
+
+module attributes {hacc.target = #hacc.target<"Ascend950PR_9579">} {
+  func.func @paged_decode_fd_kernel(%arg0: memref<?xi8>, %arg1: memref<?xi8>, %arg2: memref<?xf16> {tt.divisibility = 16 : i32, tt.tensor_kind = 0 : i32}, %arg3: memref<?xf16> {tt.divisibility = 16 : i32, tt.tensor_kind = 0 : i32}, %arg4: memref<?xf16> {tt.divisibility = 16 : i32, tt.tensor_kind = 1 : i32}, %arg5: i32 {tt.divisibility = 16 : i32}, %arg6: i32 {tt.divisibility = 16 : i32}, %arg7: i32 {tt.divisibility = 16 : i32}, %arg8: i32, %arg9: i32, %arg10: i32, %arg11: i32, %arg12: i32, %arg13: i32) attributes {SyncBlockLockArgIdx = 0 : i64, WorkspaceArgIdx = 1 : i64, global_kernel = "local", mix_mode = "mix", parallel_mode = "simd", ssbuffer.inter_core_buf_count = 2 : i32, ssbuffer.intra_buf_count = 3 : i32} {
+    %c8192_i32 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 8 : i32} 8192 : i32
+    %c128_i32 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 8 : i32} 128 : i32
+    %c0_i32 = arith.constant {ssbuffer.block_id = 8 : i32} 0 : i32
+
+    scope.scope : () -> () {
+      %alloc = memref.alloc() {ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 0 : i32} : memref<8x8x16x16xf16, #hivm.address_space<cbuf>>
+      annotation.mark %alloc {effects = ["write", "read"], hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer = #hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer<0>, ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 0 : i32} : memref<8x8x16x16xf16, #hivm.address_space<cbuf>>
+      %alloc0 = memref.alloc() {ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 0 : i32} : memref<8x8x16x16xf16, #hivm.address_space<cbuf>>
+      annotation.mark %alloc0 {effects = ["write", "read"], hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer = #hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer<4>, ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 0 : i32} : memref<8x8x16x16xf16, #hivm.address_space<cbuf>>
+      %alloc_1 = memref.alloc() {ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 1 : i32} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>>
+      annotation.mark %alloc_1 {effects = ["write", "read"], hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer = #hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer<1>, ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 1 : i32} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>>
+      %alloc_3 = memref.alloc() {ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 2 : i32} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>>
+      annotation.mark %alloc_3 {effects = ["write", "read"], hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer = #hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer<2>, ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 2 : i32} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>>
+
+      %30:2 = scf.for %arg16 = %c0_i32 to %c8192_i32 step %c128_i32 iter_args(%arg17 = %c0_i32, %arg18 = %c0_i32) -> (i32, i32)  : i32 {
+        // Vector block 1 consumes the group 0 produced by the cube block 0.
+        hivm.hir.sync_block_set {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 3 : i32, ssbuffer.intraDeps = [0 : i32, 1 : i32]}[<VECTOR>, <PIPE_V>, <PIPE_FIX>] flag = 4
+        %memspacecast_1 = memref.memory_space_cast %alloc_1 {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.crossCoreDeps = [0 : i32, 0 : i32], ssbuffer.intraDeps = [0 : i32, 1 : i32]} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>> to memref<128x128xf32>
+        // Vector block 1 produces the group 1 consumed by the cube block 2.
+        %reshape_1 = tensor.empty() {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32} : tensor<8x8x16x16xf16>
+        hivm.hir.copy ins(%reshape_1 : tensor<8x8x16x16xf16>) outs(%alloc0 : memref<8x8x16x16xf16, #hivm.address_space<cbuf>>) {ssbuffer.block_id = 1 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 0 : i32, ssbuffer.crossCoreDeps = [1 : i32, 1 : i32]}
+        // Vector block 3 consumes the group 2 produced by the cube block 2.
+        hivm.hir.sync_block_set {ssbuffer.block_id = 3 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 3 : i32}[<VECTOR>, <PIPE_V>, <PIPE_FIX>] flag = 4
+        %memspacecast_3 = memref.memory_space_cast %alloc_3 {ssbuffer.block_id = 3 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 2 : i32, ssbuffer.crossCoreDeps = [2 : i32, 0 : i32]} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>> to memref<128x128xf32>

+      scope.return
+    } {hivm.tcore_type = #hivm.tcore_type<VECTOR>}
+
+    scope.scope : () -> () {
+      %alloc_c = memref.alloc() {ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 0 : i32} : memref<8x8x16x16xf16, #hivm.address_space<cbuf>>
+      annotation.mark %alloc_c {effects = ["write", "read"], hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer = #hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer<0>, ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 0 : i32} : memref<8x8x16x16xf16, #hivm.address_space<cbuf>>
+      %alloc_c1 = memref.alloc() {ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 1 : i32} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>>
+      annotation.mark %alloc_c1 {effects = ["write", "read"], hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer = #hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer<1>, ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 1 : i32} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>>
+      %alloc_c2 = memref.alloc() {ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 2 : i32} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>>
+      annotation.mark %alloc_c2 {effects = ["write", "read"], hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer = #hivm.tightly_coupled_buffer<2>, ssbuffer.block_id = 9 : i32, ssbuffer.transfer_id = 2 : i32} : memref<128x128xf32, #hivm.address_space<ub>>
+
+      %20:2 = scf.for %arg16 = %c0_i32 to %c8192_i32 step %c128_i32 iter_args(%arg17 = %c0_i32, %arg18 = %c0_i32) -> (i32, i32)  : i32 {
+        // Cube block 0 produces the group 0 consumed by the vector block 1.

+// RUN: triton-opt --add-control-flow-condition %s | FileCheck %s --implicit-check-not=scf.while
+
+// The normal preload scheme is only enabled for the kernels whose pipeline
+// dependency is a single chain of four computation blocks that alternates the
+// cores. The pipeline also has to be a linear chain: a block that two blocks
+// feed is a merge, and the merge has two entry blocks, so the conditions of
+// the scheme do not model it.
+//
+// This kernel has the dependency chain of the test
+// pattern-kernel-conditions.mlir:
+//   cube block 0 -> vector block 1 -> cube block 2 -> vector block 3
+// and a second cube block that feeds the same vector block:
+//   cube block 4 -> vector block 1
+// The two chains share the blocks 1, 2 and 3, so they are two views of one
+// pipeline, but the pipeline has two entry blocks: the kernel keeps the
+// conditions of the upstream implementation, the main loop stays an scf.for
+// and the blocks handshake through PIPE_S. The implicit check forbids the
+// scf.while of the normal preload scheme.
+
+// CHECK-LABEL: func.func @pattern_merge_entries_kernel_conditions
+
+// The upstream scheme: the main loop stays an scf.for, the flags of the
+// blocks are published through the PIPE_S handshake.
+// CHECK: hivm.hir.sync_block_set[<VECTOR>, <PIPE_S>, <PIPE_S>] flag = 15
+// CHECK: hivm.hir.sync_block_wait[<VECTOR>, <PIPE_S>, <PIPE_S>] flag = 15
+// CHECK: hivm.hir.sync_block_wait[<CUBE>, <PIPE_S>, <PIPE_S>] flag = 15
+// CHECK: hivm.hir.sync_block_set[<CUBE>, <PIPE_S>, <PIPE_S>] flag = 15

+// The blocks that open a dependency chain are on the first level of their

+// crosses the cores. Every block of a level is compared with the blocks of
+// the higher levels of the same core:

+//   n == 1 : c_Bn - c_Bm <= m - n + (buffer_num - 1)
+//   n >  1 : c_Bn - c_Bm <= m - n

+// The first level of the core is the one that fills the buffers, it may run
+// buffer_num - 1 rounds further ahead than the other levels.

+// not numbered at all: it takes no place in the order.

+//   cube block 0 -> vector block 4 -> cube block 1 -> vector block 6

+//            consumed by the cube block 1

+// RUN: triton-opt --add-control-flow-condition %s | FileCheck %s
+
+// A block that has neither a cross-core nor an intra-core interaction is a
+// pure scalar computation: it does not exchange any data with the other
+// blocks. It is not part of the flag chain of the loop: it neither takes the
+// flag of the loop as a condition nor updates it. The chain passes through it,
+// the block that comes after it still reads the flag of the last block that
+// took part in the chain.
+//   block 1 produces attribute group 1 (three producers)
+//   block 2 consumes group 1 and produces group 0
+//   block 3 is a pure scalar computation, it has no dependency at all
+//   block 4 consumes group 0
+
+// CHECK-LABEL: func.func @pure_scalar_block
+// CHECK: scf.while
+// CHECK: ^bb0
+// The flag of the loop starts with a constant zero.
+// CHECK: %[[FLAG:.*]] = arith.constant 0 : i32
+// The first block of the chain reads the flag the loop starts with: its check
+// is always true and is left out.
+// CHECK: %[[GUARD1:.*]] = arith.andi %{{.*}}, %{{.*}}
+// CHECK: %[[IF1:[0-9]+]]:2 = scf.if %[[GUARD1]]
+// The flag of the loop is computed with a select after the block.
+// CHECK: ssbuffer.if = 1 : i32}
+// CHECK: %[[ONE1:.*]] = arith.constant 1 : i32
+// CHECK: %[[FLAG1:.*]] = arith.select %[[GUARD1]], %[[ONE1]], %[[FLAG]] : i32
+// The second block of the chain checks the flag of the first one.
+// CHECK: %[[FLAGCMP2:.*]] = arith.cmpi eq, %[[FLAG1]], %{{.*}} : i32
+// CHECK: %[[GUARD2:.*]] = arith.andi %{{.*}}, %[[FLAGCMP2]]
+// The flag of the second block is cumulative: it takes the flag of the first
+// block as its false value.
+// CHECK: ssbuffer.if = 2 : i32}
+// CHECK: %[[ONE2:.*]] = arith.constant 1 : i32
+// CHECK: %[[FLAG2:.*]] = arith.select %[[GUARD2]], %[[ONE2]], %[[FLAG1]] : i32
+// The third block is a pure scalar computation: it does not check the flag of
+// the loop and it does not update it, the chain passes through it.
+// CHECK: %[[GUARD3:.*]] = arith.cmpi slt, %{{.*}}, %{{.*}} : i32
+// CHECK: %[[IF3:[0-9]+]] = scf.if %[[GUARD3]] -> (i32) {
+// CHECK: hivm.hir.copy {{.*}} {ssbuffer.block_id = 3 : i32}
+// CHECK-NOT: arith.select

commits.message:
[TritonToLinalg](fix) preserve prefixes for loop-indexed point selects (#3176)

* [TritonToLinalg](fix) preserve prefixes for dynamic point selects

On 950, dynamically selecting one element from a loop-carried score
vector uses direct slices and regresses mix_fused. Use zero-start prefix
reconstruction for these regions while preserving direct slices for
larger regions and static offsets.

Keep the bounds guard and constant-tail buffer reuse. Cover loop-carried
point updates and static points in the dual-target lowering test.

Signed-off-by: KanuaK <yihan_z@qq.com>

* [TritonToLinalg](fix) restrict point prefixes to loop indices

The dynamic-singleton prefix fallback also catches reduction-derived
positions in TopK. With the same NPU IR toolchain, it increases the
latency of the three measured TopK cases by 149-191%.

Limit the fallback to a single-element region indexed directly by an
scf.for induction variable, looking through index casts only for source
classification. Preserve the actual cast value in slices and bounds
checks, and explicitly exclude integer iter_args from the induction
variable check.

Keep direct slices for data-dependent positions and larger regions.
Cover both mix_fused select roles, carried positions, loop-indexed matrix
rows, and reduction-derived TopK positions. Describe the measured
behavior without asserting a general scalar-copy cost on Ascend 950.

Signed-off-by: KanuaK <yihan_z@qq.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: KanuaK <yihan_z@qq.com>
